commandList:
List of commands used in the PARAM.in file for MFLAMPA configured as the SP component of the SWMF.
#ORIGIN 2.5 ROrigin [Rs] 0.0 LonMin [deg] -70.0 LatMin [deg] 360.0 LonMax [deg] 70.0 LatMax [deg]
Origin points on the surface R=ROrigin in the intervals of longitude, (LonMin,LonMax) and latitude, (LatMin,LatMax). Originating from these points are the magnetic field lines traced down from ROrigin to RScMin and up from ROrigin to RIhMax.
#PARTICLEENERGYUNIT keV ParticleEnergyUnit
The particle energy unit: for example, keV, MeV, GeV, etc. We use keV as the default value.
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! STAND ALONE PARAMETERS !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
#STARTTIME 2000 iYear 3 iMonth 22 iDay 10 iHour 45 iMinute 0 iSecond
This command can only be used in the first session.
The #STARTTIME command sets the date and time in Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) or Universal Time (UT) when the simulation starts.
There is no default value.
#SETREALTIME 2000 iYear 3 iMonth 22 iDay 10 iHour 45 iMinute 0 iSecond
This command can only be used in the first session and stand alone mode.
Detailed descriptions are very similar to the ones in #STARTTIME, but here it is with check_stand_alone.
#TIMEACCURATE T IsTimeAccurate
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
Allows solving steady-state distribution (cosmic rays, seed population) by setting IsTimeAccurate to .false., implying that IsSteadyState is .true. in the code.
#TIMESIMULATION 1 SPTime [sec]
This command can only be used in the first session.
The SPTime variable contains the simulation time in seconds relative to the initial time set by the #STARTTIME command. The #TIMESIMULATION command and SPTime are saved into the restart header file, so the simulation can be continued from the same time. This value can be overwritten by a subsequent #TIMESIMULATION command if necessary.
In SWMF the MFLAMPA time is checked against the global SWMF simulation time.
The default value is SPTime=0.
#NSTEP 100 nStep
This command can only be used in the first session.
Set nStep for the component. Typically used in the restart.H header file. Generally it is not inserted in a PARAM.in file by the user, except when the number of steps are reset for extremely long runs, such as the operational run at NOAA SWPC, to avoid integer overflow.
The default is nStep=0 as the starting time step with no restart.
This command is allowed in stand alone mode only for the sake of the test suite, which contains these commands when the framework is tested.
This command is allowed in stand alone mode only for the sake of the test suite, which contains these commands when the framework is tested.
#SAVERESTART F DoSaveRestart -1 DnSaveRestart -1.0 DtSaveRestart
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
Determine whether and when to save the restart file (STAND ALONE ONLY) Set default value as: False, -1, and -1.0
#INCLUDE run_steady/SP/restartIN/restart.H NameIncludeFile
The NameIncludeFile parameter contains the name of the file to be included. The file name may be followed with a trailing comment if it is separated with at least 3 spaces or one TAB character.
The #INCLUDE command can be used anywhere in the parameter file, even in the sections which contain the component specific parameters.
For example, the information in the run/SP/restartIN/restart.H file or parameters specific to a component can be included.
#RUN
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
The #RUN command does not have any parameters. It signals the end of the current session, and makes MFLAMPA execute the session with the current set of parameters. The parameters for the next session start after the #RUN command. For the last session there is no need to use the #RUN command, since the #END command or simply the end of the PARAM.in file makes MFLAMPA execute the last session.
#END
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
The #END command signals the end of the included file or the end of the PARAM.in file. Lines following the #END command are ignored. It is not required to use the #END command. The end of the included file or PARAM.in file is equivalent with an #END command in the last line.
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! !!!!!!!!!!!!!!! STOPPING CRITERIA !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
The commands in this group only work in stand alone mode.
#STOP -1 nIterMax 600.0 TimeMax [sec]
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
The nIterMax variable contains the maximum number of iterations {\it since the beginning of the current run} (in case of a restart, the time steps done before the restart do not count). If nIteration reaches this value the session is finished. The TimeMax variable contains the maximum simulation time relative to the initial time determined by the #STARTTIME command. If tSimulation reaches this value the session is finished.
Using a negative value for either variables means that the corresponding condition is not checked.
The #STOP command must be used in every session.
#CHECKSTOPFILE T DoCheckStopFile
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
If DoCheckStopFile is true then the code checks if the MFLAMPA.STOP file exists in the run directory. This file is deleted at the beginning of the run, so the user must explicitly create the file with e.g. the "touch MFLAMPA.STOP" UNIX command. If the file is found in the run directory, the execution stops in a graceful manner. Restart files and plot files are saved as required by the appropriate parameters.
The default is DoCheckStopFile=.true.
#ECHO T DoEcho
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
If DoEcho is true then the code set the parameters to be echoed
The default is DoEcho=.false.
#CPUTIMEMAX 3600 CpuTimeMax [sec]
This command is only used in stand alone mode.
The CpuTimeMax variable contains the maximum allowed CPU time (wall clock time) for the execution of the current run. If the CPU time reaches this time, the execution stops in a graceful manner. Restart files and plot files are saved as required by the appropriate parameters. This command is very useful when the code is submitted to a batch queue with a limited wall clock time.
The default value is -1.0, which means that the CPU time is not checked. To do the check the CpuTimeMax variable has to be set to a positive value.
Parameters of the Lagrangian grid used in MFLAMPA
#CHECKGRIDSIZE 1000 nParticleMax 4 nLat 4 nLon
This command can only be used in the first session.
Check if the configured parameters of the Lagrangian grid match those assumed in the input files, which will usually be called in RESTART.
#GRIDNODE 4 nLat 4 nLon
This command can only be used in the first session.
Set the configured parameters of the Lagrangian grid, where nLat and nLon will be placed uniformly on the solar surface, for the field line footpoints.
#GRIDNODESTART 0 iLatOffset 0 iLonOffset
This command can only be used in the first session and in the standalone mode
Set the configured parameters of the Lagrangian grid, where iLatOffset and iLonOffset denote the offset index for fieldlines along latitudes and longitude, respectively. Default values are 0.
#TESTPOS 1 iNodeTest 99 iParticleTest 1 iPTest
This command can only be used in the first session.
Set the numbers for test node, position, and momentum.
#TESTTRIANGULATE T TestTriangulate 190.0 XLocTestTri [AU] 100.0 YLocTestTri [AU] 5.0 ZLocTestTri [AU]
This command can only be used in the first session.
Set the interpolated location in the unit of [AU] to test triangulation.
#TESTPOS F UsePoleTriangulation T UsePlanarTriangles
This command can only be used in the first session.
Set options when making TRIANGULATION: (1) whether we manually include the north and south poles. Recommended to do if there are too few points; (2) whether we use planar or spherical triangles. Recommended to have spherical triangles if we set a specific radius.
#SPREADGRID 6 nSpreadLon 6 nSpreadLat
Set the size of angular grid in longitude and latitude
#SPREADSIGMA const SigmaMode 5.0 Sigma [deg]
Set the sigma changes to the lines: SigmaMode is const: all line have the same characteristic spread SigmaMode is linear-lon: sigma changes linear by lines' longitude index SigmaMode is linear-lat: sigma changes linear by lines' latitude index SigmaMode is bilinear: sigma changes bilinear by lon and lat indexes Then we set the "Sigma" of the lines, namely the changes in degrees.
#SPREADSOLIDANGLE -1.0 RadiusRef [Rs] -1.0 Sigma [deg]
Set reference radius and value of solid angle associated with lines.
#COORDSYSTEM HGI TypeCoordSystem
This command can only be used in the first session.
Type of heliocentric coordinate system used in MFLAMPA (HGI, HGR, HGC).
#MOMENTUMGRID 100 nP
This command can only be used in the first session.
Read the number of energy bins, usually from the restart.H file.
#ENERGYRANGE 1.0E+1 EnergyMin 1.0E+7 EnergyMax
This command can only be used in the first session.
Read energy range with the unit of keV as default, usually from the restart.H file.
#PITCHANGLEGRID 1 nMu
This command can only be used in the first session.
Read the pitch angle information, determine whether we take the averaged value over all pitch angles. Also, we need to specify how many intervals in the range of [-1, 1] for pitch angle.
#FLUXINITIAL 0.01 FluxInitIo [pfu]
This command can only be used in the first session.
Distribution is initialized to have integral flux: default value is set as 0.01 [pfu]. One can set this to a lower order of magnitude, e.g., 1.0E-5 pfu.
#ECHANNEL 6 nFluxChannel INT 5 1.0E+4 EChannelIo_I [MeV] INT 10 1.0E+4 EChannelIo_I [MeV] INT 30 1.0E+4 EChannelIo_I [MeV] INT 50 1.0E+4 EChannelIo_I [MeV] INT 60 1.0E+4 EChannelIo_I [MeV] INT 100 1.0E+4 EChannelIo_I [MeV]
This command can only be used in the first session.
This is to set the self-defined flux channels. As default, the code uses the 6 channels of GOES. By setting self-defined flux channels, one will not use any satellite channels unless setting #ECHANNELSAT.
For each self-defined energy channels, one needs to specify the type of flux, namely integral or diffential intensity, in the first input of EChannelIo_I. Then, one also needs to input the lower and upper bounds, in the unit of MeV, of the energy channel which the particle flux is integrated or averaged (differentiated) as the output. All the channels for fluxes saved in MH_data will be saved into MH_data_EChannel.H file.
In MH_data and MH_data_EChannel.H files, the energy channels will be saved as flux_ChannelXX, from 01 to the summed nFluxChannel. Current maximum number of energy channels is 99.
#ECHANNELSAT 1 nFluxChannelSat GOES NameSatellite
This command can only be used in the first session.
This is to set the energy channels of specified satellites or instruments for convenient comparisons with observational data. These energy channels and also flux types, i.e., integral or differential intensity, have already been written in the module, according to the energy bins from the original websites of observational data. By specifying satellites, one do not have to type each energy channel in #ECHANNEL (Of course, this is the alternative way to achieve this). All the channels for fluxes saved in MH_data will be saved into MH_data_EChannel.H file.
If one does not specify anything, either by #ECHANNEL or #ECHANNELSAT, we will use the 6 energy channels of GOES as default. If one specifies #ECHANNEL and still wants to include the satellite energy channels, one needs to explicitly specify #ECHANNELSAT in this case. When including both #ECHANNEL and #ECHANNELSAT, the self-defined channels will always be set ahead of the satellite energy channels in the outputs.
In MH_data and MH_data_EChannel.H files, the energy channels will be saved as flux_ChannelXX, from 01 to the summed nFluxChannel. Current maximum number of energy channels is 99.
#LOWERENDBC inject TypeLowerEndBc
For different cases of TypeLowerEndBc, different LowerEndSpectrum_I values are used in diffusion.
For LowerEndSpectrum_I, it is the spectral extrapolation following the power law of SpectralIndex at the lower boundary when TypeLowerEndBc = "inject". Besides, one can set "float" (= current VDF at iVertex=1) and "escape" (= Background_I), especially for the steady-state GCR spectrum simulations.
#UPPERENDBC lism TypeUpperEndBc usoskin TypeLisBc T UseModulationPot 600.0 ModulationPot
For different cases of TypeUpperEndBc, different UpperEndSpectrum_I values are used in diffusion.
As for UpperEndSpectrum_I, we need to first determine the type of UpperEndBc, where LISM is the nominal one for use. If one wants to turn off the UpperEndSpectrum_I, TypeUpperEndBc should be set to "false" with no differences in lower and upper cases. For LISM, there are various models fitting or simulating the spectrum, read as TypeLisBc. Here we set Eq.(2) in Usoskin et al. 2005 as default. Then, we also need to determine whether we use LISM or the GCR spectrum at 1-2 AU. For the latter one, we also need the modulation potential (denoted as "phi" in Usoskin et al. 2005), which is temporal- and spatial- (and even energy-) dependent. We stick to the one derived by Oulu neutron monitor and published in the "Dataset 1" on https://cosmicrays.oulu.fi/phi/phi.html.
#MOMENTUMBC inject TypeMomemtumMinBc 5.0 SpectralIndex 1.0 EfficiencyInj escape TypeMomemtumMaxBc
Set up parameters for the momentum boundary condition, controlling the types of BC at injection/minimum and maximum particle energies or its equivalent momentum.
Once can set "inject" as TypeMomemtumInjBc for injecting particles, e.g., for SEP simulations and read parameters of the power-law spectrum of suprathermal particles at sqrt(2*mp*Ti) lt p lt Pinj:
f(p) propto [Efficiency * (Spectral index - 3) / p**SpectralIndex]
The injection efficiency is the ratio of suprathermal proton density to the total proton density. Should not exceed one, however, somewhat higher than one values may be of use. Default distribution is f(p) propto [1.0 * 2 / p**5].
However, in other cases like for background GCRs, there is no need to inject particles. Then, one can set "float"/"floating"/"escape" for a floating/escape boundary at injection/minimum energy/momentum, meaning to set f(iP=0) = f(iP=1). One can also set "grad" to use the same gradient, i.e., grad:f(iP=0) to f(iP=1) remains the same as grad:f(iP=1) to f(iP=2) in geometric scale.
It is the same for the maximum energy/momentum by setting TypeMomemtumMaxBc. Any other type is regarded as an unrecognized one at this stage.
#CFL 0.9 Cfl
The CFL number for explicit scheme solving, for example, advection along energy axis in the phase space.
#ADVECTION F UsePoissonBracket
If UsePoissonBracket is True, the advection scheme is conservative Poisson bracket scheme; otherwise, it is non-conservative.
This will be implemented later: parameter name="UseMuFocusing" type="logical" default="F"
The default value is false.
#FOCUSEDTRANSPORT F UseBetatron F UseInertialForce F UseMuScattering
When choosing to solve the focused transport equation, one should configure SP/MFLAMPA with nMu greater than 1; otherwise, there will be a warning and stop for the run.
When solving the focused transport equation, we keep including the adiabatic focusing in the magnetic field (with such, we first have energy consevation), and the first-order Fermi accleration. One can also specify more terms of interest for the simulation, such as the betatron accleration (D(lnB)/Dt /= 0) and the inertial force (Du/Dt /= 0), by setting parameters of UseBetatron and UseInertialForce, respectively, in the PARAM.in file.
In the focused transport equation solver, one can also determine whether to include the scattering term for pitch angle. If so, the coefficients (e.g., DMuMu and LamdbaMuMu) will be set up and the scattering with pitch angles will be included. One can also determine whether to solve the spatial diffusion by setting UseDiffusion in #DIFFUSION.
The default values for both of these parameters are false.
#RESTART T DoRestart
The default value is true.
#DORUN T DoRun
If DoRun is False, only magnetic field lines are extracted, but the particle distribution function is not solved.
The default value is true.
#TRACESHOCK T DoTraceShock
If DoTraceShock is False, the shock wave is not traced and the density profile is not sharpened around it, which means that there is no shock accleration process involved.
The default value is true.
#IDENTIFYSHOCK 10 nShockWidth 50 nShockMargin 0.01 dLogRhoThreshold
These parameters are used to identify the shock location: we use iShock-nShockWidth+1:iShock+nShockWidth to identify the minimal divU, which should be smaller than -dLogRhoThreshold. In this process, one should notice that the shock should not be too close to the end, so there is a number of nShockMargin settign for the "margin" distance.
#DIFFUSIONPARA F UseBtotal sokolov2004 TypeMhdDiffusion
UseBtotal is for the turbulence calculation: when calculating (B/dB)**2, if UseBtotal=.true., B is given as sqrt(B**2+dB**2). The default value is false, and one can turn this on. TypeMhdDiffusion is to determine how the turbulence (dB) is calculated from the MHD parameters. "giacalone1999" assumes a (dB)**2/(1+(k*lc)**(5/3)) law for the power spectral density in the turbulence spectrum. "sokolov2004" is what we use from the Sokolov et al 2004 paper, assuming Ic*k**(-5/3) law with a correlation length setup in "ScaleTurbulence1AU".
#USEFIXEDMFPUPSTREAM T UseFixedUps 0.3 MeanFreePath0InAu
UseFixedUps is to determine whether we set the mean free path in upstream, with formulas described Li et al. (2003), doi: 10.1029/2002JA009666. The default value for UseFixedMeanFreePathUpstream is set as as false, and that for MeanFreePath0InAu is 0.3 [AU], one can also see Chen et al. (2024), doi: 10.3847/1538-4357/ad33c3.
#DIFFUSION T UseDiffusion
Used for testing, to disable diffusion, which by default is true.
#SCALETURBULENCE const ScaleTurbulenceType 0.3 ScaleTurbulence1AU [AU]
The cut-off wavenumber of turbulence spectrum is k0 = 2*cPi/Scale. The default value is set as const (or constant), i.e., the value (e.g., 0.3 AU) of "ScaleTurbulence1AU" in the unit of [AU].
#TURBULENTSPECTRUM F UseTurbulentSpectrum
Determine whether we use the turbulence spectrum. Set the default value is false.
#USEDATETIME T UseDateTime
Set the format for the output file names like _eYYYYMMDD_HHMMSS tagging the file with real date and UT tume instant. When unset (default) the time tag looks like _tHHMMSS, where HHMMSS is the simulation time in hours- minutes-seconds passed after the initial time (set by the command #STARTTIME)
#TIMING T UseTiming -2 nTiming -1 nDepthTiming cumm TypeTimingReport
Set the timing format in SP component, but as default, we set UseTiming as False; if UseTiming is True, one should specify nTiming, nDepthTiming, and TypeTimingReport. nTiming is set to be -2 as default: greater than -3 means that it reports the time at each specified spot; greater than -2 means that it reports the time in each TIMELOOP; greater than 0 is needed, to show the timing results, if required (with speed as cells/second/PE/step).
#SAVEINITIAL T DoSaveInitial
As the default (DoSaveInitial=T) the MFLAMPA saves datasets (at least the MHD information) starting from the initial state prior to the run. However, once MFLAMPA restarts, it is useful to set DoSaveInitial to F, in order to avoid rewriting the output files and eliminate duplicate tags in the file tag list, becuase the same output files and tags were saved at the end of previous run.
#READMHDATA T DoReadMhData MH_data/ NameInputDir
Sets the name of input directory with MHD data.
#MHDATA idl TypeFile 120 nFileRead MH_data.lst NameTagFile
Sets type and format of the MHD input files. nFileRead and NameTagFile are always read but only used when UseAppendedRead is false in #READMHDATA.
#APPENDMHDATA F UseAppendedRead F UseAppendedWrite
Controls the format of MH_data input and output files. Both default to false and this command is optional. If UseAppendedRead is true, each field line is read from a single file with all time steps appended (MH_data_iLon_iLat.out). If UseAppendedWrite is true, all time steps for each field line are appended to a single output file (MH_data_iLon_iLat.out). The file is overwritten on the first write and appended to on subsequent writes. Note: input and output directories must be different when both UseAppendedRead and UseAppendedWrite are true.
#NTAG 120 nTag
The number of different time-line tags of the MH_data files.
#SATELLITE 4 nSatellite ../TRAJECTORY/earth.dat NameTrajectoryFile ../TRAJECTORY/sta.dat NameTrajectoryFile ../TRAJECTORY/psp.dat NameTrajectoryFile ../TRAJECTORY/solo.dat NameTrajectoryFile
This command can only be used in the first session.
Set the satellites included for spectra outputs along the trajectory. nSatellite is the number of the satellite trajectory, TypeCoordSystem is the type of the coordinate system specified for the outputs and plotting same as in SP, and NameTrajectoryFile is the path of the trajectory file.
#SAVEPLOT 11 nFileOut mh1d flux ascii StringPlot mh2d flux ascii StringPlot 215.0 Radius [Rs] (read if mh2d/mhtime/distr2d/distrtime/flux2d/fluxtime) mhtime flux ascii StringPlot 215.0 Radius [Rs] (read if mh2d/mhtime/distr2d/distrtime/flux2d/fluxtime) distr1d momentum length cdf ascii StringPlot distr1d energy distance def idl StringPlot distr2d energy def idl StringPlot 215.0 Radius [Rs] (read if mh2d/mhtime/distr2d/distrtime/flux2d/fluxtime) distrtime energy def idl StringPlot 215.0 Radius [Rs] (read if mh2d/mhtime/distr2d/distrtime/flux2d/fluxtime) distrtraj def energy idl StringPlot flux2d flux ascii StringPlot 215.0 Radius [Rs] (read if mh2d/mhtime/distr2d/distrtime/flux2d/fluxtime) fluxtime flux ascii StringPlot 215.0 Radius [Rs] (read if mh2d/mhtime/distr2d/distrtime/flux2d/fluxtime) 30.0 Longitude [deg] (read if fluxtime) 46.0 Latitude [deg] (read if fluxtime) shock2d ascii StringPlot
Sets the number and type of the plotfiles to save. For several types of plot, the radius of heliocentric spherical surface on which to plot may be also set. As a simple example, the #SAVEPLOT above show how to write the StringPlot to save all the formats we provide at the current stage. One can include more strings for the properties in between for each StringPlot. One also need to pay attention, that "mh1d" can only be saved once (appear once in #SAVEPLOT).
Again, as an example, "mh1d" means to save 1D plot (for each magnetic field line) including coordinates and MHD variables; "R" means radial coordinate (R) plus fluxes; "idl" means to save the data in the idl format. Particularly, the "mh1d", "mh2d", "mhtime", "flux2d", and "fluxtime" save the integral particle intensity in the unit of p.f.u., for the Lon-Lat contour, along the time axis, with MHD data saved or not, respectively.
For the differential particle intensity in the unit of p.f.u. per energy unit, "distr1d" saves all the values of the VDF (each momentum, at each coordinate along each fieldline), "distr2d" saves the VDF at fixed heliocentric distances for all fieldlines, "distrtime" saves the VDF at fixed radius along the timeline for each fieldline, and "distraj" only saves the VDF values interpolated to the specified satellite trajectories.
For "distr1d", "cdf" represents the canonical distribution function, "def" means the differential energy function (intensity), saved in the unit of [#/cm**2/s/sr/energy unit], i.e., [pfu/energy unit], and "DEF" is to save the differential energy function in the unit of [#/m**2/s/sr/energy unit]. Here, the "energy" or "momentum" is the first axis, for the log10(kinetic energy) in the specified unit (default: keV) or the log10(momentum) normalized by the injection momentum, respectively. The "distance" or "length" is the second axis saved in the unit of solar radii, for the heliocentric distance or the field line length to the foot point on the Sun, respectively. If nMu is not 1, i.e., solving the focused transport equation with anisotropic pitch angles, there will also be one axis for mu's value right after the momentum/energy axis in the "distr*"-formatted outputs, and the MhData integral flux is then the one averaged over all calculated pitch angles.
For "distr2d", the StringPlot format is basically the same as it is in "distr1d", except that we do not use distance or length. Instead, one need to specify the radius for interpolating and saving the distribution function. This is also applicable to the parameters used for "distrtime".
If using "distraj", one should also specify "#SATELLITE" and reset, "#TRIANGULATION" including 'UsePoleTriangulation' (default = F) and 'UsePlanarTriangles' (default = T) before these lines.
In normal cases, one should have at least 3 parameters for each StringPlot. However, if using "shock*", one should just have 2 parameters: save format and extension. "Shock2d" is to save outputs for Lon-Lat contour plot at each time step, while "ShockTime" is to save outputs along the time axis for each field line.
In StringPlot, the first identifier is always a type of plot, the last identifier is a type of file, and the string variables in between denote the list of plot variables extra to the MHD ones.
A Jupyter notebook comparing the differential (Distr*) and integral (Mh*) particle intensity outputs is SP/MFLAMPA/Scripts/mflampa_crosscheck.ipynb, which shows the absolute and relative differences are both very tiny and demonstrates these two types of outputs are consistent.
Please send an email to Igor Sokolov for more information on this command.
#NOUTPUT 10 nOutput -1.0 DtOutput
Frequency to plot: iteration or simulation time. This option is to output the results more frequently than the couple time, so the DtOutput is at most the couple time in SWMF runs.
